title: Finite Kummer coefficients and normalization of scalar-forgetting maps
statement:
Fix the finite-field and coefficient data of [def-pur-conventions], write $e=e(E/\mathbf Q_\ell)$, assume $e\mid n$, and set $N=n/e\geq1$, $r=\ell^N$ and $R=\mathbf Z/r\mathbf Z$. Then $rA=0$, $A$ is a finite free $R$-algebra, and $r$ is invertible on every $k$-scheme. Choose a primitive $r$-th root $\zeta\in k$. For every $k$-scheme $T$, on its small etale site put $L_T=\mu_{r,T}\otimes_{R_T}A_T$, with the roots and tensor sheaves of [def-sc-kummer-sequence], [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product]. There are isomorphisms
$$R_T\xrightarrow{\sim}\mu_{r,T},\quad a\longmapsto\zeta^a,\qquad A_T\xrightarrow{\sim}L_T,\quad a\longmapsto\zeta\otimes a,$$
compatible with every $k$-morphism $u:T'\to T$ through the canonical inverse-image coefficient identifications. In particular $L_T$ is pulled back from $\operatorname{Spec}k$ and its underlying finite abelian group has order a power of $\ell$.

For a unit $v\in\Gamma(T,\mathcal O_T)^\times$, define $\kappa_{T,A}(v)=H^1(z\mapsto z\otimes1_A)(\delta_T(v))$, where $\delta_T$ is the connecting map of the ordinary exact $r$-Kummer sequence, with the cohomology-pullback convention of [def-weil-pbc-cohomology-pullback]. Then
$$u^*\kappa_{T,A}(v)=\kappa_{T',A}(u^*v).$$
The assertion concerns the ordinary Kummer sequence before extension of coefficients, and requires no $R$-module structure on $\mathbf G_m$.

All these maps may be computed in module sheaves or in their underlying abelian sheaves: the canonical comparisons of [lem-weil-pbc-etale-module-cohomology-forget], [lem-sbc-higher-direct-image-forget-comparison] identify constants, coefficient maps, cohomology pullbacks and resolution-induced maps, for global cohomology and every higher direct image in all integer degrees. More explicitly, for a morphism $a:X\to B$ and a sheaf $F$ of $A$-modules, they identify $U_B\mathcal H^q(Ra_*F)$ with $\mathcal H^q(Ra_*U_XF)$, where $U$ forgets scalars, and identify the underlying groups of $H^q(X,F)$ with $H^q(X,U_XF)$. For every cartesian square the comparisons intertwine the actual module-derived exchange with the abelian-derived exchange, as specified in [lem-weil-pbc-exchange-forget-coefficients]. They reflect invertibility of the module maps.

proof.text: Apply [lem-pur-finite-kummer-level] with the given divisibility hypothesis: $N=n/e\geq1$, $\ell^NA=0$ and $A\cong R^{ef}$ as $R$-modules. The quotient ring map makes this a finite free $R$-algebra. Since $k$ has characteristic $p\ne\ell$ [def-pur-conventions], the scalar $r$ has an inverse in $k$, whose image is an inverse on every $k$-scheme. [lem-sc-primitive-root] supplies $\zeta$ and the distinct roots $\zeta^a$, $a\in R$.

source.place: Opening paragraph: finite coefficient level and primitive root

proof.text: Here is the sheaf trivialization on an arbitrary $k$-scheme, including nonreduced schemes. The roots sheaf has the unit-valued description in [lem-asd-etale-finite-twist-pullback]. For any etale test $V$ and root $z$, the factorization $z^r-1=\prod_{a\in R}(z-\zeta^a)=0$ gives the open cover $V_a=\bigcap_{b\ne a}D(z-\zeta^b)$: in each residue field exactly one factor vanishes, because differences of distinct $\zeta^a$ are units. On $V_a$ all the other factors are invertible, so $z=\zeta^a$. Distinct labels cannot agree on a nonempty overlap. Thus roots are exactly locally constant labels in $R$, with powers corresponding to addition. By the constant-sheaf and sheafification descriptions [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf], [lem-pc-sites-sheafification-underlying-sets], this proves the claimed $R_T$-linear isomorphism $a\mapsto\zeta^a$. The factorization uses the $r$ distinct roots of [lem-sc-primitive-root].

source.place: Opening paragraph: primitive root trivializes the finite root sheaf

proof.text: Tensor the preceding isomorphism with $A_T$ using [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product]. The explicit inverse to $a\mapsto\zeta\otimes a$ sends $\zeta^b\otimes a$ to $ba$; the tensor balancing relation proves that both composites are identities. For a $k$-morphism $u$, the canonical comparisons of [lem-asd-etale-finite-twist-pullback] pull a root back by its unit-section formula and pull constants back to the same constants. Hence they take $\zeta^b$ to $\zeta^b$ and $\zeta^b\otimes a$ to $\zeta^b\otimes a$. This proves compatibility of both trivializations. Apply this also to $T\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ to obtain the claimed pullback description. Its constant coefficient group is the additive group of $A\cong R^{ef}$ from step 1, of order $r^{ef}$, a power of $\ell$. This assertion is about the coefficient group, not all global sections on a disconnected $T$.

source.place: Opening paragraph: trivialization after coefficient extension and its pullback compatibility

proof.text: By [lem-amb-kummer-any-base], the ordinary $r$-Kummer sequence is short exact on each small etale site, since $r$ is invertible. Let $c:u^{-1}\mathbf G_{m,T}\to\mathbf G_{m,T'}$ be adjoint to pullback of units. Pulling back units commutes with $r$th powers: $(u^*z)^r=u^*(z^r)$. Consequently $(c_\mu,c,c)$ is a morphism from the inverse-image Kummer sequence to the Kummer sequence on $T'$, where $c_\mu$ is the canonical root comparison of [lem-asd-etale-finite-twist-pullback]. The pullback ladder [lem-weil-pbc-pullback-cohomology-long-exact-ladder] commutes with the first boundary. Naturality for the morphism $(c_\mu,c,c)$, $H^1(c_\mu)\delta_{u^{-1}S}=\delta_{S'}H^0(c)$ on $T'$, is clause (1) of [lem-weil-pbc-horseshoe-delta-functor] for the horseshoe connecting maps of $v=\Gamma(T',-)$; by [lem-sc-p1-right-derived-triangle-connecting] these are the connecting maps of the triangle obtained by applying $R\Gamma(T',-)$ to the triangle of the short exact sequence, i.e. the maps $\delta_{T'}$ of the ladder. Composing these two identities, and using [lem-weil-pbc-cohomology-pullback-degree-zero] to identify $H^0(c)u^*$ on units, gives $H^1(c_\mu)u^*\delta_T(v)=\delta_{T'}(u^*v)$. No inverse-image isomorphism for $\mathbf G_m$ is asserted.

source.place: Tag 03PL, lemma-kummer-sequence; Tag 04I0, section-functoriality; cohomology.tex Tags 01F8 and 01FB

proof.text: Write $i_T:\mu_{r,T}\to L_T$, $z\mapsto z\otimes1_A$, and $c_L:u^{-1}L_T\xrightarrow{\sim}L_{T'}$. On the generators of the sheafified tensor product, $c_L\circ u^{-1}i_T=i_{T'}\circ c_\mu$, by the root and coefficient identifications already established. Apply the naturality clause of [lem-weil-pbc-cohomology-pullback-functorial] to $i_T$, then substitute step 4: $H^1(c_L)u^*H^1(i_T)\delta_T(v)=H^1(i_{T'})H^1(c_\mu)u^*\delta_T(v)=H^1(i_{T'})\delta_{T'}(u^*v)$. These are exactly the two stated Kummer classes. The boundary was formed in abelian sheaves first; only its value is mapped by $i_T$. Thus no action of $R$ on $\mathbf G_m$ occurs.

source.place: Step 3: Kummer boundary and coefficient extension commute with pullback

proof.text: Forgetting module structure is exact by [lem-weil-pbc-module-sheaves-colimits-forgetful]. Constants and their maps agree with their abelian versions: apply [lem-cbc-module-sheafification-underlying-sets] to the constant module presheaf and [lem-pc-sites-sheafification-underlying-sets] to its underlying abelian presheaf. Both comparison maps extend the identity on constant sections; uniqueness of sheafification identifies them, including addition and scalar maps. The same argument applies to the sheafified insertion $i_T$, so its underlying coefficient map is precisely $z\mapsto z\otimes1_A$, rather than a map modified by an automorphism of the coefficient line.

source.place: Tag 00YR, section-sheaves-algebraic-structures, clauses (gamma) and (epsilon); sites-modules.tex Tags 03DA and 03DB

proof.text: For global cohomology use the natural isomorphism [lem-weil-pbc-etale-module-cohomology-forget]. For $a:X\to B$ use the fixed unit-compatible derived comparison [lem-weil-pbc-module-abelian-derived-direct-image-comparison]; its cohomology is the comparison of [lem-sbc-higher-direct-image-forget-comparison], in every integer degree. These choices fix the maps, as follows. If $F\to I^\bullet$ is a bounded-below module injective resolution and $UI^\bullet\to J^\bullet$ an abelian K-injective replacement, the comparison is represented by $\Gamma(I^\bullet)\to\Gamma(J^\bullet)$, respectively $a_*UI^\bullet\to a_*J^\bullet$. Module injectives are underlying-global-section acyclic by [lem-weil-pbc-etale-module-injective-forget-acyclic], so the former computes the stated global comparison. For any chosen resolution lift $b$, naturality gives $\chi_{F'}H^q(b)=H^q(Ub)\chi_F$. For a pullback along $u$, [lem-weil-pbc-module-abelian-inverse-image-comparison] identifies the underlying module unit with the abelian unit; compose this unit identity with the unit-compatible direct-image comparison and the resolution maps defining $u^*$ in [lem-weil-pbc-cohomology-pullback-functorial]. Taking global sections and $H^q$ gives the same identity for cohomology pullback. Thus coefficient maps and all the resolution-induced maps agree under the specified comparisons. For $q<0$ the sheaves placed in degree zero and their right derived images have zero cohomology, so the same assertions hold there.

source.place: Tag 03FD, lemma-cohomology-modules-abelian-agree; Tag 072W, lemma-higher-direct-images; Tag 0D6J, lemma-modules-abelian-unbounded, canonical comparison construction

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-exchange-forget-coefficients] to each cartesian square with $\Lambda=A$ and $K=F[0]$. Its equality identifies the actual module-derived exchange with the abelian-derived exchange under the very inverse- and direct-image comparisons used in step 7, and gives the exchange invertibility assertion. For any other module sheaf map, if its underlying abelian map is invertible, its sectionwise inverse is automatically $A$-linear: for $y=f(x)$, $f^{-1}(ay)=f^{-1}(f(ax))=ax$. Hence forgetting reflects invertibility. On complexes its exactness from step 6 identifies cohomology before and after forgetting; thus it reflects quasi-isomorphisms as well. This proves the final reflection assertion for the module-derived maps too.
